featured_reviews.name: umair shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I purchased my new Royal Enfield Bullet 350 from this showroom and while the sales process initially felt smooth, the overall buying and delivery experience turned out to be disappointing.

When I first visited the showroom on 6th March 2026 to book the bike, I specifically asked about the delivery timeline. The salesperson told me the bike could be delivered within 10–15 days and even said, “humlog sirf bolne ke liye 30 din bolte hai.” I clearly asked whether it would be possible to get the bike before 30th March 2026, and I was assured that it should be delivered before that date.

Based on that assurance, I booked the bike and waited. However, till around 25th March, I received absolutely no update from the showroom. I had to personally call and follow up myself, only to then be informed that the delivery was delayed and they did not know how long it would take because it was an MIY (Make It Yours) order.

What was disappointing was the lack of communication and updates from the showroom. Throughout the process, I was the one constantly following up instead of the showroom proactively informing me about the status of the bike.

Finally, I received delivery of the bike on 16th April 2026, much later than the timeline that was promised during booking. Even at the time of delivery, the number plate was still not available. I eventually took delivery without the number plate because I did not want to leave the motorcycle at the showroom any longer after already waiting so much.

Unfortunately, the problems did not end there.

During delivery itself, I noticed multiple visible issues on a brand-new bike — the rear mudguard was tilted towards the right side, the reflector below the tail light was off-center, and even the clutch and brake levers were not aligned properly. These are basic fitting and alignment issues that should have been identified and corrected during the pre-delivery inspection before handing over the motorcycle to the customer.

When I pointed these problems out before delivery, I was told that the service centre would fix everything later. As a customer spending around ₹2.5 lakhs on a new motorcycle, I do not expect to take delivery of a bike with noticeable fitting issues from day one.

The disappointing part was the lack of coordination between the showroom and service centre. The showroom staff kept saying it was the service centre’s responsibility, while the service centre kept shifting responsibility back to the showroom. This resulted in multiple visits, wasted hours, and unnecessary frustration for a brand-new bike that was not even a month old.

The brake squeaking issue is still unresolved and I was simply told “isme aese hi awaz ayegi.” That is not the kind of ownership or support a customer expects after purchasing a premium motorcycle.

I expected much better delivery quality, inspection standards, communication, and customer handling from Royal Enfield. Customers should not have to repeatedly argue just to get obvious issues acknowledged and corrected after purchasing a new vehicle.

Overall, the buying experience started positively, but the delayed delivery, poor communication, weak pre-delivery inspection, and disappointing post-delivery support made the overall experience frustrating.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Its a review for JAWA overall.
I'm telling you guys it's not worth it I'm telling you as an owner of perak since 11 months.

Buying a bike is an investment for long term so don't go with "love at first sight" theory.
No doubt the bike is head turner but that's only one aspect that most of the people give too much weight weightage on.

It is after getting it that I got into disadvantages that hit me really hard.

The rust issue- within few months rusting started from bolts to handle to cable springs of brake to rear disc brake to silencer pipe.
Because of rust I had to change whole disc pads and brake disc which itself cost around 5.5k rupees. (It's not covered in insurance ofcourse)

The suspension is too hard although it's adjustable the rear ones but still it's not sufficient, even a mild(not exaggeration) pot hole in road will shake you up literally to spine.

The clutch issue- I've tried tweaking the clutch but still doesn't solve the mysterious sudden engine halt randomly during ride.

The rear indicators- they are so flimsy it falls out of its socket and you won't even know, when I asked to stabilize it in service center, they says fix it with "feviquick"..Really???!

The after service- let me tell you everything can be forgiven if the issues are dealt professionally after all which bike doesn't have issues, but the after service of jawa once you have bought it PATHETIC, absolutely unprofessional. I'm based in mumbai and I have dealt with atleast 3 authentic service centers. The people over there are truly unprofessional, a roadside mechanic would be far better in professionalism. I cannot overemphasize on this part, people assume jawa as a premium bike company and buy it because of brand but they should recruit aftersale service men carefully, once you take your bike to them you feel like you have bought some cheap bike looking at those crooks looting and befooling you of your hard earned money.
Based on only this factor alone I wouldn't suggest anyone to buy a jawa bike.

(Mind you, I have mailed, messaged, chatted online, called numerous times regarding these to their executive all in vain)

Puncture issue- it's an issue which we have to deal eventually, perak built is such that repairing puncture for roadside mechanics find it difficulty and when I called service center they plainly refuse to do it saying puncture can be attended by normal mechanics.

Even the parts/accessories are really difficult to get on time even in service center in mumbai. I was without side stand spring and tail light for so many days just because they had to order such simple parts from idk where??

I know it's an accumulated frustration from a perak owner but hope to save as much people as possible from future investment into jawa.
